artifacts.summary: Incident ticket opened with initial logs

items.text:
## Description

The bot service outage was detected on **2024-03-15T14:27:03Z** on node **10.42.7.18**. David Silva pulled the deployment logs from `/shared/incident/bot-service/logs/` and identified a brief error burst that aligns with commit **a1b2c3d4e5f6**. Karen Lee streamed real‑time counters from `/shared/incident/bot-service/metrics.json` and is correlating them with the root‑cause dump placed in `/shared/incident/bot-service/analysis/`. A hot‑fix revert is being prepared and will be pushed to staging within the next 15 minutes, after which traffic will be flipped and the bot service instance will be restarted. All artifacts remain in the restricted folder as a draft‑review copy; please do not forward outside the incident response team.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy the faulty handler from commit **a1b2c3d4e5f6** to node **10.42.7.18**.
2. Observe the error burst in `/shared/incident/bot-service/logs/` around **2024-03-15T14:27:03Z**.
3. Monitor the real‑time counters in `/shared/incident/bot-service/metrics.json` for latency spikes.
4. Revert the commit and redeploy the previous stable version to staging, then flip traffic back to the restored instance.

## Investigation

- **David Silva** cross‑referenced the deployment log diff with the real‑time counters and pinpointed the race condition in the new handler introduced by commit **a1b2c3d4e5f6**.
- **Karen Lee** continues streaming counters and will flag any post‑revert anomalies; her findings will be saved under `/shared/incident/bot-service/analysis/`.
- **Leon Marchetti** will assist with the staging rollout verification once the hot‑fix is applied.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The hot‑fix revert is successfully pushed to staging and traffic is flipped without triggering new errors.
2. Real‑time counters return to baseline levels for at least 10 minutes after the flip.
3. No error bursts are recorded in `/shared/incident/bot-service/logs/` for the next 30 minutes.
4. All relevant artifacts remain in the restricted folder and are marked as draft‑review copy.

## Next steps

- **David Silva** to push the revert to staging within the next 15 minutes and trigger the traffic switch.
- **Karen Lee** to monitor counters for any resurgence of spikes and update the analysis folder.
- **Leon Marchetti** to validate the restarted bot instance and confirm service health.
- Once the restart is verified, close the incident ticket and archive the logs in the restricted folder.

items.text:
## Agenda

- Review hot‑fix deployment plan and confirm revert steps
- Assign ownership for staging rollout and traffic flip
- Define post‑fix monitoring criteria and validation responsibilities
- Plan incident ticket closure and artifact archiving

## Discussion

David Silva opened the meeting by recapping the root‑cause analysis: the error burst aligns with commit **a1b2c3d4e5f6** observed at **2024-03-15T14:27:03Z** on node **10.42.7.18**. He confirmed that a hot‑fix revert is ready to be pushed to staging. Karen Lee, though absent, will continue streaming real‑time counters from `/shared/incident/bot-service/metrics.json` and will flag any post‑revert anomalies in the restricted folder. Leon Marchetti agreed to verify the bot instance restart and to watch the counters for a 10‑minute baseline after traffic is flipped. The team reiterated the acceptance criteria from the ticket – successful staging push, traffic flip without new errors, and stable counters for at least 10 minutes. All participants acknowledged that the artifacts remain in the restricted folder as a draft‑review copy and must not be forwarded externally.

## Decisions

- Deploy the hot‑fix revert to staging and flip traffic immediately after push
- Restart the bot service instance on node 10.42.7.18 as part of the fix
- Leon Marchetti will validate the restarted instance and confirm service health
- Close incident ticket TKT-049-M1A2 once verification is complete

## Action items

- Push hot‑fix revert to staging and flip traffic — owner: David Silva; due: 2026-02-11
- Validate restarted bot service instance and report status — owner: Leon Marchetti; due: 2026-02-11
- Monitor real‑time counters for a 10‑minute baseline post‑flip — owner: Leon Marchetti; due: 2026-02-11
- Update incident ticket TKT-049-M1A2 with closure note and final metrics — owner: David Silva; due: 2026-02-11
- Archive all logs, analysis files, and metrics in the restricted folder as a draft‑review copy — owner: David Silva; due: 2026-02-12

**Temporary rollback plan (if we see a regression):**

3. Flip traffic back to that version and restart the bot instance on the same node. 
4. Monitor counters for a fresh 10‑minute baseline; if they stay steady we’ll consider the rollback successful and move to a more permanent fix.

artifacts.summary: Post‑mortem document detailing root cause and mitigation steps

items.text:
## Summary

A concise root‑cause analysis of the bot service outage, the corrective actions taken, and the final decision to close the incident ticket after verification.

## Root‑Cause Summary

The outage was traced to a race condition introduced by commit **a1b2c3d4e5f6** deployed on **2024-03-15T14:27:03Z** to node **10.42.7.18**. 

* **David Silva** cross‑referenced deployment logs from `/shared/incident/bot-service/logs/` with real‑time counters in `/shared/incident/bot-service/metrics.json` and identified the brief error burst that aligned with the faulty handler. 
* **Karen Lee** streamed live counters and confirmed no latency spikes beyond the burst window, storing all observations in `/shared/incident/bot-service/analysis/`. 
* The race condition was isolated to the new handler introduced in the aforementioned commit, which caused intermittent request failures during the rollout.

## Mitigation Steps Executed

1. **Hot‑Fix Revert** – A revert to the pre‑a1b2c3d4e5f6 version was pushed to staging and traffic was flipped within 15 minutes (see ticket **TKT-049-M1A2**). 
2. **Service Restart** – The bot instance on node **10.42.7.18** was restarted immediately after the traffic flip (action led by **David Silva**). 
3. **Validation** – **Leon Marchetti** verified the restarted instance, confirming that real‑time counters remained at baseline for over 10 minutes and no new error bursts appeared in `/shared/incident/bot-service/logs/`. 
4. **Monitoring** – **Karen Lee** continued streaming metrics from `/shared/incident/bot-service/metrics.json` for an additional hour, logging any deviation in `/shared/incident/bot-service/analysis/`. 
5. **Archival** – All logs, diff analyses, and rollback instructions were archived under `/shared/incident/bot-service/` as a draft‑review copy in the restricted folder.

## Final Decision and Responsibility

The incident ticket **TKT-049-M1A2** is now **closed** after verification of service health. 
The final decision **"Close incident ticket after verification"** is attributed to **Leon Marchetti** (ML Engineer). 
All related artifacts remain in the restricted folder and are marked as a draft‑review copy; they must not be forwarded outside the incident response team.
